fact_text: The analyst assigns Pakistani cement capacity a replacement value of USD 45-65 per ton depending on profit per ton, driven by royalty exposure, coal usage and electricity or alternative fuel mix, a spread worth about 40% in valuation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: As a rough benchmark the analyst gives a cement plant with a 30% operating profit margin about USD 60 per ton of value, and one nearer 20% about USD 45-50 per ton.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In peak boom cycles Pakistani cement valuations have reached around USD 80 per ton, as happened in 2007 and again in 2016.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst anchors cement fair value at about USD 60 per ton because that level is reached in a merely reasonable market rather than a peak bull market, which builds in a margin of safety.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Greenfield cement expansion costs roughly USD 80-90 per ton to build, yet listed Pakistani cement rarely trades above USD 60-70 per ton outside negotiated plant sales, so the sector usually sits below replacement cost.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst values full nameplate capacity, defined as output if plants run about 300 days, but caps the per-ton value near USD 70; using today's low utilisation with a higher per-ton value gives a similar answer.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Efficient Pakistani cement plants earn roughly USD 15-20 of profit per ton once depreciation is added back, against the USD 100 per ton valuations that fully utilised plants command internationally.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because a fair value calculation sums five to ten years of profits, the analyst uses an average utilisation of roughly 70-75% rather than the current year's lower figure.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Across Pakistan cement plants as a whole, production rarely exceeds about 60-65% of installed capacity.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In theory a higher-utilisation cement plant deserves a higher assigned value, but in practice large players cannot push volumes without starting a price war that destabilises the whole market, so they do not.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A genuine cement sector boom only arrives when utilisation approaches 80%, which needs a real estate upturn, so the sector can lag a broader stock market bull cycle by a year or two.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Running a cement kiln far below capacity damages it, so multi-line producers run one or two lines at full load and idle the oldest; Maple Leaf runs its 2 million and 3 million ton lines near 100% with the oldest line shut.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A single-line cement company facing 50% demand must repeatedly stop and restart its only kiln, losing efficiency, whereas a two-line rival simply runs one line continuously.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: South region plants export even at thin margins so they can keep running at full load; Lucky exported about 3 million tons against South capacity of roughly 4.5 million tons, effectively running it flat out.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: No Pakistani cement company draws more than about 10-15% of its electricity from solar, and even including wind the practical ceiling is 30-40%, because renewables need land, produce nothing at night and need fossil backup.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Solar capacity helps a cement plant proportionally more when it is running at low utilisation, because the cheap solar units then cover a larger share of total consumption before dearer sources are needed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst applies accounting materiality to diversification news: Kohat's roughly PKR 750 million property investment is under 1% of the company, so even a 100% return on it would not move fair value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Plant visit comments about a new venture may describe the sponsor group rather than the listed company, so the analyst checks which entity would actually hold the business before giving it any value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Over a ten to twenty year holding period an investor's return converges on the business's return on invested capital, while over two or three years it comes mainly from closing an under or overvaluation gap.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Power Cement genuinely turned around and is earning good margins, but years of accumulated losses leave net debt so large that even a USD 45 per ton valuation leaves little upside once liabilities are netted off.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Sponsor loans parked inside equity should be added to net debt when valuing a company, because the sponsor intends to take that money back and minority shareholders will never receive it.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst bridges from a per-ton capacity valuation to equity value by subtracting total liabilities less current assets, which is what kills the upside in heavily indebted small cement names.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Gharibwal's sponsors hold about 90% of roughly 400 million shares, so a PKR 1 dividend used to send them around PKR 350 million.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Once super tax applied, Gharibwal's sponsors faced roughly 50% combined tax on dividends against 35-39% on salary, so from 2023 onwards they drew money as pay and admin costs rose sharply.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Sponsor salaries of that size matter at Gharibwal because the plant is only about 2 million tons; the same amount drawn from a 10 million ton company would barely dent minority shareholders' earning power.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst saw Gharibwal as mildly undervalued but required far more upside before preferring it to better-placed peers, given weaker efficiency, high sponsor salaries and a small free float.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Gharibwal plans an expansion that would take it to four or five million tons in a year or two, after which the analyst says it would warrant the same analysis as the larger producers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Beyond normal construction demand, a national mega project such as a large dam can be big enough to justify new cement plants being built nearby.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Ordinary Portland cement dominates Pakistani sales and every producer exports and holds ISO certification, so product mix differences such as pozzolana or sulphate-resistant grades do not change the valuation model.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Punjab cement companies provisioned the full limestone royalty amount throughout the year they held a Lahore High Court stay, so losing the case creates no extra charge in later results.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Where a company holds a court stay but has not booked the disputed liability, an adverse judgement lands as a single large one-off charge, so the analyst checks whether the provision has actually been taken.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Power Cement's export business grew strongly and its plant efficiency changed, which the analyst treats as a real fundamental shift worth re-examining despite the balance sheet.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Don't Buy Cement Stocks Before Understanding This!' (YouTube transcript, undated)
